66.0.0.en: 1- Make a joyful noise unto God, all ye lands: 2- Sing forth the honour of his name: make his praise glorious.

66.0.1.en: 1- The author of the psalm calls on all people to shout to God, that is, to declare their joy with jubilation and praise, and to sing forth, that is, to continue in prayers of joy, glorifying God for His great works, whether His forgiveness of their sins if they offer repentance, or their rescue from afflictions, as He brought the captives back from Babylon to Jerusalem and they built the temple, or for the resurrection of Christ from the dead, to proclaim to humanity victory over the devil and new life.

66.0.2.en: 2- The singing and the shouting are for the glory of the name of God, not for our personal glory, and singing is the highest of prayers, because it asks nothing for man, but is only for the glory of God. Singing is with the lips, and also with good works.

66.1.0.en: 3- Say unto God, How terrible art thou in thy works! through the greatness of thy power shall thine enemies flatter thee.

66.1.2.en: Flatter thee: deceive thee and lie to thee.

66.1.3.en: 1- The author of the psalm teaches people, when they shout to God, to say to Him, How terrible are Your works, and how great, whether in His great creation or in His rescue of His people, such as bringing them out of Egypt with the ten plagues, their crossing of the Red Sea, and how He provided for them with manna and quail from heaven, and water from the rock!

66.1.4.en: 2- When the pagans see the great works of God they fear Him greatly, so they flatter Him, that is, they lie, declaring their submission to Him, and then draw back from this outward faith, as Pharaoh declared his submission to God during the ten plagues, and then went back and hardened his heart.

66.2.0.en: 4- All the earth shall worship thee, and shall sing unto thee; they shall sing to thy name. Selah.

66.2.1.en: 1- All the earth means all humanity, that is, Jews and Gentiles. This is a prophecy about the faith of the Gentiles, who will come and worship in submission to God, declaring their faith. Then they will be able to sing to His holy name.

66.2.2.en: 2- This passage ends with the word Selah, which is a musical pause for meditating on the greatness and glory of God.

66.2.3.en: Do not deprive yourself of the joy of praising God, so that you rise above earthly things and are drawn toward the love of God, and feel His presence with you and long for heaven, and walk spiritually in your steps on earth.

66.3.0.en: 5- Come and see the works of God: he is terrible in his doing toward the children of men. 6- He turned the sea into dry land: they went through the flood on foot: there did we rejoice in him.

66.3.1.en: 1- The author of the psalm, by the Holy Spirit, calls on those who have believed and praised God to look with their hearts at the great works of God that He did with His people, such as the parting of the Red Sea and turning its bed into dry land, and likewise the parting of the river Jordan and making its bed also dry land, so that the children of Israel were able to walk on it with their feet and cross to the other bank. The Holy Spirit always calls us to see with our hearts, and to recall and remember with our minds God's works with us. This brings us into a wonderful feeling of joy, so we rejoice as God's people rejoiced of old when they crossed the Red Sea and the river Jordan. This crossing is a symbol of Baptism, by which we crossed from death to life, so we remain in constant joy.

66.3.2.en: 2- When we remember God's great works in parting the sea and the river we rejoice, although the event did not happen to us, and it is supposed that those to whom it happened rejoiced; but all of us who believe in God rejoice together, so we rejoice in God's works of old, and the present ones that happen with us, and even those of the future, that is, we rejoice in the faith of those who have not yet believed, and this shows the unity of the Church through the generations.

66.4.0.en: 7- He ruleth by his power for ever; his eyes behold the nations: let not the rebellious exalt themselves. Selah.

66.4.1.en: 1- It appears from the preceding verses that God has power and authority over the whole earth, and if some do not believe in Him and resist, God's eyes watch them, so that if they rebel He punishes them, as happened with Pharaoh when he increased his humiliation of God's people and became very proud, and God struck him with the ten plagues and then drowned him in the sea. One who rebels against God cannot exalt himself above God, but God is long-suffering and gives him an opportunity to repent, and if he does not repent He takes vengeance on him.

66.4.2.en: 2- At the end of this passage there is the word Selah, which is a musical pause for meditating on the power and authority of God, so that we may fear Him and keep away from every sin.

66.4.3.en: When you read the Holy Bible and see the great works of God, offer Him thanks and glorification, confident that God is the same yesterday, today and forever, so your heart will be at peace and rejoice, and your praise of Him will increase.

66.5.s.en: (3) Praise of the Chastener and Healer

66.5.0.en: 8- O bless our God, ye people, and make the voice of his praise to be heard:

66.5.1.en: The author of the psalm calls on those of the Gentiles who have believed to bless God, our God, that is, the God of the Jews who believe in Him, and then asks those of the Gentiles who have believed to make the sounds of their praises heard by those around them, whether those who have believed, that they may be firm in their faith, or those who have not yet believed, that they may call them to faith. Making their voices heard is not only with the lips, but rather with works, and also with proclaiming God's works and His wonders with them.

66.6.0.en: 9- Which holdeth our soul in life, and suffereth not our feet to be moved.

66.6.2.en: God gave man life when He breathed into him the breath of life, and created him from dust, and then gave him the commandment to live by. When he fell, He gave him the promise of life, that the seed of the woman would bruise the head of the serpent (Gen 3:15). Then He fulfilled the promise of life by His Incarnation, His redemption and His resurrection, so Christ became our life, and by His power He protects us from falling into sin, and if we fall He raises us up. By our constant steadfastness in Christ our Rock our feet will not slip.

66.7.0.en: 10- For thou, O God, hast proved us: thou hast tried us, as silver is tried. 11- Thou broughtest us into the net; thou laidst affliction upon our loins.

66.7.2.en: 1- In His concern for His children, God permits trials for them to purify them from all evil, as silver is refined to separate it from impurities and dross, so that the children of God become pure from all the filth of sin.

66.7.3.en: 2- Likewise God permits afflictions for His children, that they fall into the net of the enemies, and He also lays heavy burdens on their backs, until they almost fall from the weight of the load, as He permitted His children to be humiliated in Egypt before He freed them by the hand of Moses, and likewise the humiliation of captivity in Assyria and Babylon before He brought them back to their land.

66.8.0.en: 12- Thou hast caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water: but thou broughtest us out into a wealthy place. Continuing God's chastening of His children, He permitted their enemies to rule over them, as happened in Egypt in the days of Moses, when the enemies rode over the heads of the children of Israel and humiliated them; but the grace of God intervened, and after they were almost destroyed, drowning in the humiliation of forced labor and the fire of slavery, God brought them out with a high hand, after He struck the Egyptians with the ten plagues and made His people pass through the Red Sea, and they were not drowned, but Pharaoh and his army were drowned, and they crossed the wilderness of Sinai, and He brought them into the land of Canaan, the fertile land flowing with milk and honey.

66.8.1.en: Bear afflictions, for they are temporary and many blessings follow them; they also deliver you from your sins, and you live in repentance, and you learn virtues from them, such as humility, faith and prayer.

66.9.s.en: (5) The praise of those who fear God

66.9.0.en: 16- Come and hear, all ye that fear God, and I will declare what he hath done for my soul. 17- I cried unto him with my mouth, and he was extolled with my tongue.

66.9.2.en: 1- The author of the psalm speaks to those who fear God, because whoever fears God keeps away from sin, is purified, and is able to praise God. The author tells them of the works of God, not only those He does with His people, such as the crossing of the Red Sea and the crossing of the river Jordan (v. 6), but he also tells them of God's works with him, so he cries out praising and glorifying God with his tongue; that is, the works of God are ancient and contemporary, and in every generation His children feel His great works with them and glorify Him.

66.9.3.en: 2- He tells those who fear God of God's works with him, that they may join him in glorifying God, because the power of God is the cause of every blessing in the life of the author of the psalm and of all who fear God, and therefore God must be glorified.

66.10.0.en: 18- If I regard iniquity in my heart, the Lord will not hear me: 19- But verily God hath heard me; he hath attended to the voice of my prayer.

66.10.2.en: 1- The author of the psalm declares a necessary condition for the answering of prayer, which is repentance from every sin; but whoever persists in sin, or is lax with it, or justifies it, so that it remains in his heart, God does not answer him. Man's weakness does not hinder God's work, but persisting in sin and treating it as permissible is what angers God, so He does not listen, and God does not answer such prayers.

66.10.3.en: 2- When the author here does not regard iniquity in his heart, this is not out of pride, but because he walks in the way of God, so he repents at once of every sin. He entreats God with humility, need and repentance.

66.11.0.en: 20- Blessed be God, which hath not turned away my prayer, nor his mercy from me. In conclusion the author of the psalm blesses God for two things:

66.11.2.en: 2- God's mercies that He poured out upon him, which include his inner peace, his love for God, and his rescue from many troubles ...

66.11.3.en: The acceptance of prayers is also part of God's mercy, and therefore at the end of every matter we must thank God and bless Him.

66.11.4.en: Hold fast to the fear of God so that you may be purified from your sins, and your prayers may rise to God and He answer them, and you may enjoy His abundant mercies.

66.11.5.en: The joy of the Gentiles in salvation. To the Chief Musician on Neginoth. A Psalm. A Song. "God be merciful unto us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us" (v. 1) Introduction:

66.11.6.en: 1- Its author is unknown, and it is therefore classified among the orphan psalms, but some attribute it to David.

66.11.7.en: 2- It is sung by a group of singers who have a leader, or chief.

66.11.8.en: 3- The recitation of this psalm is accompanied by a musical instrument called the stringed instrument, which is a string instrument like the lute.

66.11.9.en: 4- We see in the title of the psalm that it is a song; it is thanksgiving and praise to God from His beloved who believe in Him, and an invitation to the whole world to join in praising Him.

66.11.10.en: 5- This psalm is a clear prophecy about the faith of the Gentiles in Christ and their praise of Him.

66.11.11.en: 6- This psalm is considered liturgical, for in the Old Testament it was recited at the Feast of Harvest, or Pentecost, and it was also recited at the Feast of Tabernacles. It was called the psalm of blessing, since the word blessing is repeated in it three times.

66.11.12.en: 7- The first verse of this psalm is recited at the conclusion of the Evening and Morning Raising of Incense.

66.11.13.en: 8- This psalm is found in the Agpeya in the prayers of Prime and the Sixth Hour, so that the day may begin with blessing, and likewise in the Sixth Hour the world received the blessing through the crucifixion of Christ and His redemption of it.

67.0.s.en: (1) The knowledge of God offered to all people

67.0.0.en: 1- God be merciful unto us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us. Selah.

67.0.1.en: 1- The author of the psalm asks for himself and for his people God's compassion, His mercies and His blessings, and as he comes forward with humility and need, he finds before him not God's judgment and justice, but His compassion and blessing. God shines upon him, so He sanctifies him, blesses him, and gives him spiritual understanding and the knowledge of the person of the great God.

67.0.2.en: 2- When a person receives God's blessing and compassion, he is able to give light to others, and is changed into a spiritual person, who shows compassion and mercy to those around him.

67.0.3.en: 3- These mercies and this enlightenment are accomplished in Christ incarnate in the fullness of time, who changes those who believe in Him into earthly angels who know God and convey the knowledge of Him to others.

67.0.4.en: 4- This verse ends with the word "Selah," which is a musical pause for meditating on God's tenderness, His blessings, and the knowledge with which He favors all.

67.1.0.en: 2- That thy way may be known upon earth, thy saving health among all nations.

67.1.1.en: 1- When God pours out His mercies on the world and shines upon it with His face, the world knows His way, that is, His commandments, and His salvation offered to all, the Gentiles in addition to the Jews, which is the cross and redemption.

67.1.2.en: 2- The way is Christ, who said, "I am the way" (Jn 14:6); it is He who saves those who believe in Him and brings them to the Kingdom.

67.1.3.en: Contemplate the love of Christ on the cross, for He strives for your salvation and your spiritual enlightenment. And when you contemplate, your heart is filled with reassurance, joy, and longings to know God and enjoy fellowship with Him.

67.2.s.en: (2) The faith and praise of the Gentiles

67.2.0.en: 3- Let the people praise thee, O God; let all the people praise thee.

67.2.1.en: When the peoples of the world, that is, the Gentiles, received the salvation of Christ, they raised their voices in praise and thanksgiving to God, and began to offer worship to God with the rest of the believers. All this was accomplished in the fullness of time, by the redemption of Christ, and this verse speaks in the spirit of prophecy about the spread of faith in Christ among the Gentiles.

67.3.0.en: 4- O let the nations be glad and sing for joy: for thou shalt judge the people righteously, and govern the nations upon earth. Selah.

67.3.1.en: 1- The Gentiles who believed in Christ and worship Him remain in a state of continual joy in fellowship with Him, especially since they enjoy the guidance of God, who is upright in judgment, so He judges them and governs them with truth, unlike the people of the world, who are liable to error, deviation and partiality.

67.3.2.en: 2- God seeks the Gentiles who have not yet believed, preaching to them to guide them to Himself, that they may believe and join the rest of those of the Gentiles who have believed in worshiping God and praising Him. And when the day of judgment comes He judges them righteously, so they receive the glories of the Kingdom, but the wicked and unbelievers are cast into eternal torment.

67.3.3.en: 3- This verse ends with the word "Selah," which is a musical pause for meditating on God, the Pantocrator, before whom we shall stand on the day of judgment.

67.4.0.en: 5- Let the people praise thee, O God; let all the people praise thee.

67.4.1.en: After the joy of the Gentiles who believed in Christ over His salvation and worship of Him, they were also reassured that the just Judge on the day of judgment is Christ Himself, their God, who will bring them into the Kingdom, so they thank God every day for all that He has prepared for them in heaven.

67.4.2.en: If only you would thank God every day for His salvation, and for the Kingdom He has prepared for you, so that your heart rises above sin and the material things of the world and clings to the love of God, who gave you Himself on the cross, and gives you to taste His sweetness on earth, and will give you what you cannot imagine in the Kingdom.

67.5.s.en: (3) The blessing of God and the fear of Him

67.5.0.en: 6- Then shall the earth yield her increase; and God, even our own God, shall bless us.

67.5.1.en: 1- This psalm was written at the time of harvest; therefore the author of the psalm declares that this yield is the blessing of God given to His children to satisfy their needs. It shows God's care for His children.

67.5.2.en: 2- The earth signifies human beings, and the yield is their faith in Christ; this is the true blessing that God gives to people. The earth also signifies human beings, among whom is the Virgin Mary, so the yield is the fruit of her womb, that is, Christ who was born of her.

67.6.0.en: 7- God shall bless us; and all the ends of the earth shall fear him.

67.6.1.en: 1- When people see that God is the cause of the blessing that gives them life, they trust that their life is in His hand, so they fear Him, and the fear of Him keeps them from sin and purifies their hearts, so they behold Him while still on earth and enjoy fellowship with Him.

67.6.2.en: 2- When people enjoy God's material blessings on earth they thank Him, incline to every good work, prepare for the day of judgment, and live every day in the fear of God.

67.6.3.en: What is the yield you produce? It is the spiritual fruits, so examine yourself: do you carry out the commandment, and does it appear in your life? Then you will be a light to the world and the salt of the earth.

67.6.4.en: God the Savior of His people and the avenger on His enemies. To the Chief Musician. A Psalm of David. A Song. "Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him" (v. 1) Introduction:

67.6.7.en: a- When David brought up the ark of the covenant of God from the house of Obed-edom the Gittite (2 Sam 6:12-15).

67.6.8.en: b- David wrote it in the spirit of prophecy about future events such as God's victories in the days of King Hezekiah over Sennacherib (2 Chr 32:20-23), or the last years of the Babylonian captivity, or the victories of the Maccabees in the second century before Christ.

67.6.9.en: 3- Moses, when moving the tabernacle of meeting and journeying from one place to another, used to recite the beginning of this

67.6.10.en: 4- This psalm is one of the Messianic psalms, because it speaks of the life of Christ on earth and His resurrection and ascension.

67.6.11.en: 5- St. Paul the Apostle quoted (v. 18) in the Epistle to the Ephesians (Eph 4:8).

67.6.12.en: 6- The beginning of this psalm (v. 1) is quoted in the Litany of the Assemblies in the Divine Liturgy, and is also found at the beginning of the Midnight prayer.

67.6.13.en: 7- This psalm does not occur in the prayers of the Agpeya.
